subject: FinTechCo pricing follow-up: US vs EU region costs and token economics
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + follow-up: tokens, budget target, US vs EU residency

Hey Mark great chat this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope a clean quote: 

Summary from call:
- Expected token volumes: pilot ~20M tokens/month (1-2 months), ramp to production ~120M tokens/month.
- Peak concurrency: ~60 qps (inferred from expected traffic patterns).
- Primary workload: real-time text generation (customer support responses) + periodic batch embeddings for search.

Clarifying asks to finalize pricing:
1) Can you confirm the long-term expected monthly tokens (we used 120M as the target for production sizing)? Any seasonality?
2) Budget range / target unit economics  you mentioned a target cost per 1M tokens on the call. Can you confirm a target $/1M tokens range (ballpark is fine, we'll create scenarios)?
3) Data residency: you said EU customer data needs to remain in the EU. Is that a hard requirement for all EU-origin traffic, or only for regulated customers? That will materially affect hosting/pricing.

I attached a quick token estimate workbook (FinTechCo_token_estimate.csv) with the scenarios we discussed.

Next steps: if you can confirm the two items above (volumes + target $/1M + residency strictness) we'll produce (a) a hosted pricing quote for US vs EU region and (b) a committed (Dedicated) reserved capacity example with discount tiers.

Thanks Sean
Sean Gallagher

From: Mark Johnson <mark.johnson@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + follow-up: tokens, budget target, US vs EU residency

Sean thanks for the recap and the file. Quick answers below (forwarding to legal as well).

1) Volumes: pilot will be 15-25M/month (target 20M). Production estimate is ~120M/month with expected 20% growth Y/Y. There will be some weekly spikes but the 60 qps number looks about right.

2) Budget / target $/1M tokens: for production our procurement target is ~$1,000 per 1M tokens (we understand this is negotiable with committed terms). For the pilot we can accept higher unit costs; pilot is to validate latency and quality.

3) Data residency: EU-origin customer data must stay within the EU for regulatory (GDPR + country-specific banking regs) and privacy reasons. Non-EU data (e.g., US customers) can be processed in the US. So we need regionally segmented hosting or a deployment that guarantees EU-only processing for EU traffic.

Please put together a simple hosted vs dedicated comparison with region-specific pricing and a committed discount schedule that hits the ~$1,000/1M target at production volumes. We can share rough timeline/PO once legal signs off on data processing addendum.

-Mark

Mark / Sean looping in pricing details and regional considerations. Below are three scenarios (hosted) with ballpark unit economics; we'll refine in the formal quote and show Dedicated/reserved options with tiered discounts.

Assumptions used: model family = open-llm-13b-like; token mix = 75% generation / 25% embeddings; latency SLO = p95 < 500ms.

Hosted pricing (baseline list, per 1M tokens):
- US region (multi-az): $900 per 1M tokens
- EU region (multi-az + EU-only processing + additional encryption/KMS controls): +15% uplift = $1,035 per 1M tokens

Notes on uplift:
- EU uplift accounts for: reserved EU capacity, additional data residency controls, KMS/HSM integration overhead, and local network/cloud cost differentials (~10-20% typical).
- If you require an on-prem or fully air-gapped Private deployment for a subset of EU customers, that can be quoted but will materially increase unit costs (40-80%+ depending on scope).

Committed / Dedicated pricing (examples for 12-mo commit at 120M tokens/month):
- 12-mo commit: ~25% discount off hosted list (US) => ~$675 per 1M tokens (US)
- EU committed: list uplift then discount => ~$776 per 1M tokens (EU)

Targeting your procurement target (~$1,000 / 1M):
- Hosted EU list of $1,035/1M is slightly above target; a 12-month Dedicated commit gets you comfortably below target in EU (~$776/1M).
- Alternatively, hybrid approach: host US traffic in US (US price) and run EU traffic on Dedicated reserved capacity to meet regulatory needs and cost targets.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We'll produce a side-by-side hosted vs dedicated quote showing monthly costs at pilot (20M) and production (120M), including expected token spend and estimated monthly invoice.
2) Legal: we'll provide a DPA + outline of EU data segregation architecture for review.
3) Commercial: if this looks good we'll finalize a 12-mo committed example that hits your $/1M target and share SOW + standard terms.

I attached a short pricing workbook and the example scenarios (Redwood_pricing_estimate_20260610.xlsx). Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through.

 Lauren
